HxResult HxSpinButtonDelete ( HxSpinButton_t *  pSpinButton  ) 

Delete a spin button widget.

HxSpinButtonDelete deletes a spin button created from an earlier call to HxSpinButtonNew.

It is not necessary to call this function when quitting the application, since the widget's parent calls this function just before the parent is deleted. HxSpinButtonDelete only needs to be called when removing a spin button at runtime.

Parameters:
pSpinButton IN: Pointer to the spin button to delete
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxSpinButtonGetValue ( HxSpinButton_t *  pSpinButton,
double *  pValue 
)

Get the value of a spin button.

HxSpinButtonGetValue returns the value of a spin button.

Parameters:
pSpinButton IN: Pointer to a spin button
pValue OUT: Returns the value of the spin button
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_BUFFER_EMPTY if the spin button's field is empty. If the user has called MakeIndeterminate and the user has not hand typed a value then the field will be empty and HX_BUFFER_EMPTY will be returned.

HxResult HxSpinButtonMakeIndeterminate ( HxSpinButton_t *  pSpinButton  ) 

Set the spin button to the indeterminate state.

This blanks out the text in the control until the user types in the field. This allows for the case where the spin button is representing more then one value which are different. i.e. More then one margin in a word editor

To check if the field is currently in an indeterminate state call HxSpinButtonGetValue and check HxResult for HX_BUFFER_EMPTY.

A field leaves the inderminate state when a user types into the field or HxSpinButtonSetValue is called.

Parameters:
pSpinButton IN: Pointer to a spin button
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

Create a spin button control widget.

HxSpinButtonNew creates a new spin button control widget. The spin button attempts to keep user input values bounded by the minimum and maximum values. When the user is typing current typing which could be extended to allow it to fall within the range of valid values is extended and the extension is highlighted. If a number can't be brought into range (i.e. it is larger then the max) It is capped at either the min or the max, whichever is logical for the given case. A user backspacing through the field will force the the minimum value to be placed in the field and the field to be completely selected.

Here are some examples of usage for the formatSpecifier parameter Specifier Result Description "%.0f" 2 Integer display "%2.1f in" 2.1 in Decimal with suffix "02.0f" 02 Integer with leading 0's Intended to support leading zeros, decimal precision and suffix strings.

Parameters:
id IN: Unique ID for the widget, defined by app, or kHxWidgetAutoID to auto-generate the ID
pParent IN: Pointer to "parent" widget containing button
initialValue IN: Initial value for the spin button
minValue IN: Minimum value for the spin button
maxValue IN: Maximum value for the spin button
increment IN: Increment value for each spin button click
formatSpecifier IN: printf style format string. Only vararg is double
x IN: x coordinate for the top left button origin
y IN: y coordinate for the top left button origin
hSpinButton OUT: Handle to the new spin button; *hSpinButton is NULL on failure
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails, and sets *hSpinButton to NULL.

Reset the min and max values for a spin button.

This will reset the minValue and maxValue for the spin button. Once the min and max are reset the range is enforced.

HxResult HxSpinButtonSetValue ( HxSpinButton_t *  pSpinButton,
double  value 
)

Set the value of a spin button widget.

This function sets the value of the spin button. Attempting to set the value for the spin button outside of the minimum or maximum values will cause the input to be automatically capped to the min or max and no error is returned.

Parameters:
pSpinButton IN: Pointer to a spin button
value IN: The current value of the spin button
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.
